name: Anjali Choudhary
deck: Six hundred and seventy-seven people in Bharuch found out where their wet waste goes. Discarded chemical tanks became bulk composters, and one site now takes 180 to 200 kilos a day that used to leave for the landfill.
description: Composting units in Bharuch schools, offices and an orphanage, 677 people sensitised, and one site now taking 180 to 200 kilos of wet waste a day.

aims.h: Compost where the waste is made
aims.p: Schools, corporate campuses, an orphanage. The unit goes in on site, so the organic half of the bin never gets on a truck.
Students, self-help group women, housekeeping staff. Segregation is a habit held by the person handling it daily, not by the person who signs the policy.

aims.h: Use what is already lying around
aims.p: Discarded IBC tanks for bulk composting, a shredder for garden waste, microbes to speed it up, an earthen pot for the households who only need one.

did: Ran sensitisation sessions for 539 school students across Bharuch
Trained 98 women, including online sessions with rural self-help groups
Installed composting units at two corporate campuses and two schools
Converted discarded IBC tanks into bulk composters and put a shredder on the garden waste
Supplied compost accelerators and ran earthen-pot demonstrations for households
Gave institutions the technical know-how to keep the units running themselves

figures.label: Organic waste composted daily at one site

quotes.text: Need of the hour and how else students will learn about managing their own waste.
quotes.speaker: Nirmala Maam

holes: The unit at the orphanage was still going in when the report closed, so the sixty-five children there are counted as sensitised and not yet as composting.
